verdict.rationale: x402's own docs give merchants a self-serve path: add one line of code to gate requests behind HTTP 402, use the hosted CDP Facilitator for settlement, and receive funds at any address they control. Endpoints built with the CDP SDK are listed in the Bazaar automatically, with no registration form, and independent builders (Apiosk, httpay) run x402 endpoints. missing for 10: documented onboarding steps for the CDP API key the facilitator requires (keyless calls return 401), a step-by-step seller quickstart in the pack, and immediate discoverability, since Bazaar listing only follows a first settled payment.

support.subject: As a merchant, I have a documented self-serve path to start accepting agent traffic — enable a setting, sign an agreement, or publish an endpoint

citations.quote: Add one line of code to require payment for each incoming request.
There is no registration form or separate API call.
Sellers receive at any address they control
Getting discovered makes your endpoint available to tens of thousands of agents through CDP APIs, the Bazaar MCP server, and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
x402-enable a merchant checkout built on Payment Acceptance so agents can authorize payment sessions directly.
